atlas-jp.0152: Hand in the form for permission to work at the airport: 28 hours a week in term, 40 in vacations, never in nightlife or adult entertainment. Students can defer the national pension.
atlas-jp.0154: Unpaid internships up to 90 days fit a visa-free stay, with only documented expenses reimbursed; longer unpaid ones need Cultural Activities status. A paid internship for credit, under an agreement between your university and the company, uses Designated Activities, up to a year.
atlas-jp.0155: Job search after a Japanese degree, and J-Find
atlas-jp.0156: Graduates of Japanese universities can stay six months, renewable once, to look for work, with the university’s recommendation, and work 28 hours a week.
atlas-jp.0157: J-Find gives up to two years, with work allowed, to graduates of the last five years from universities in the top 100 of two of the QS, THE and ARWU rankings; no Italian university qualifies.
atlas-jp.0160: The usual status for graduate jobs: a degree related to the role (or 10 years of experience), pay at least equal to a Japanese colleague, for 3 months to 5 years. The employer applies for the Certificate of Eligibility, valid three months.
atlas-jp.0161: The points-based Highly Skilled Professional status (70 points) gives five years at once and permanent residence after three years, or one with 80 points.
atlas-jp.0164: Report a change of employer to immigration within 14 days.
atlas-jp.0165: Unpaid thesis visits use Student, Cultural Activities or a visa-free stay; paid researchers hold Researcher or Professor status.
atlas-jp.0166: MEXT scholarships cover tuition and flights with a tax-free monthly stipend; JSPS post-doctoral fellowships pay about 362,000 JPY a month.
atlas-jp.0169: Terms depend on your country. The Italy–Japan agreement has run since 1 April 2026: Italians resident in Italy aged 18 to 30, 500 visas a year, 12 months, once, free.
atlas-jp.0170: Work must be secondary to the holiday, and never in nightlife; motivation letters about building a career get refused.
atlas-jp.0172: The UK has its own youth scheme with Japan; the research covers the Italian agreement only, so check the British terms with the Japanese foreign ministry.
atlas-jp.0173: Up to 90 days with no paid work. Only citizens of Austria, Germany, Ireland, the UK and a few other countries can extend by another 90 days; Italians and most EU citizens cannot.
atlas-jp.0174: Your sponsor (employer or school) applies for the Certificate of Eligibility (COE) at the regional immigration office; it is issued electronically, usually in 1 to 3 months, and is valid exactly 3 months: if you do not land in time it lapses.
atlas-jp.0175: Book a registered share house, school dormitory or company housing from home: hostels, hotels and Airbnb listings are refused for residence registration.
atlas-jp.0176: Within 14 days of moving into your home, register your residence at the ward or city office (kuyakusho, shiyakusho): the clerk prints the address on the back of your residence card.
atlas-jp.0177: The residence card (zairyū card) is printed on landing only at Narita, Haneda, Kansai, Chubu, New Chitose, Hiroshima and Fukuoka; at other airports you get a passport stamp and the card comes by post after you register.
atlas-jp.0178: Students should hand in the permission form for part-time work at the immigration desk on arrival: applying later means 2 to 6 weeks without the right to work.
atlas-jp.0179: Registering your residence also issues your My Number, the personal number used for tax and social security.
atlas-jp.0180: Employees are enrolled by their company in employee health insurance and the employees’ pension, with contributions split 50:50 and withheld at source; others join the municipal National Health Insurance.
atlas-jp.0181: A card without the address on the back is not accepted for bank or phone contracts. First get a Japanese voice SIM from a provider for foreign residents that takes foreign credit cards (Mobal, Sakura Mobile, GTN Mobile).
atlas-jp.0182: Then open an account at Japan Post Bank (Yūcho), the one bank that opens ordinary accounts in your first 6 months; after 6 months, have it switched from non-resident to resident.
atlas-jp.0183: For trips abroad under a year, tick the special re-entry permit box on the embarkation card at the airport; it is free, but if you forget it, your status ends when you leave.
atlas-jp.0184: Register your address at the town hall within 14 days; hostels, hotels and Airbnb are not accepted, so book a registered share house or dormitory.
atlas-jp.0185: When leaving for under a year, tick “special re-entry permit” on the embarkation card, or your status ends at departure.
atlas-jp.0186: Most banks refuse accounts in your first six months; Japan Post Bank is the exception.
atlas-jp.0187: The Certificate of Eligibility lapses if you do not land within three months.
atlas-jp.0188: Whether working holidaymakers can switch to a work status inside Japan is left to immigration’s discretion.
atlas-jp.0189: From 2027 a new training system replaces the technical intern programme, and permanent residence can be revoked for unpaid tax or pension.
atlas-jp.0190: The digital nomad visa gives no residence card, so holders cannot register an address.
